title: Chapter 4 — PCB Interconnects: Electrical Properties, Noise and Return Path Routing

questions.question: What is an interconnect on a PCB?
options: A conductive path that electrically connects components or circuit elements
questions.explanation: Interconnects are conductive paths establishing electrical connections.

questions.question: What forms a net?
options: A group of electrically connected pins, pads, vias, and traces
questions.explanation: The chapter defines a net this way.

questions.question: What is the complete set of nets in a circuit called?
questions.explanation: The complete set of nets is the netlist.

questions.question: A net may include pins, pads, vias, and traces.
questions.explanation: All are explicitly included in the definition of a net.

questions.question: When is an interconnect considered transparent?
options: When its electrical properties have a negligible effect on the transmitted signal
Only when it is on a breadboard
questions.explanation: Transparency means negligible effect on the signal.

options: Zero resistance, zero propagation delay, and no parasitic capacitance or inductance

questions.question: Ideal schematic wires introduce no noise, distortion, crosstalk, or reflections.
questions.explanation: This follows from their ideal properties.

questions.question: Physical PCB traces are always perfectly equivalent to schematic wires.
questions.explanation: Physical traces can have non-ideal electrical properties.

questions.question: What does signal integrity (SI) describe?
options: How well a signal preserves its intended shape and timing from transmitter to receiver
How much current a PCB can carry
How mechanically strong a connector is

Measured only with a DC voltmeter
